'''Daniel Scherwin Koltun''' (December 7, 1933 – April 9, 2014) was an American [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]]. His work focused on the [[Many-body problem|many-body theory]] and [[Atomic nucleus|nuclei]] sub-components including [[meson]]s, [[pion]]s, and [[quark]]s. He created the "Koltun Sum Rule" which was used in the measurement of [[electron scattering]].

==Education==
Koltun graduated in 1955 from [[Harvard University]] with a bachelor's degree<ref name=PAW/> and in 1961 from [[Princeton University]] with a Ph.D. in physics with a thesis in ''New methods of spectroscopy applied to the nuclear 1-p shell''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=249233|name=Daniel Scherwin Koltun}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1962 he joined the [[University of Rochester]]'s physics faculty and worked there until his retirement in 2004 as professor emeritus.<ref name=PAW>{{cite journal|title=Memorial. Daniel S. Koltun *61|website=Princeton Alumni Weekly|date=4 March 2015|url=https://paw.princeton.edu/memorial/daniel-s-koltun-61}}</ref>

His research focused on nuclear structure; intermediate and high energy reactions; and the many-body theory. He studied nuclei as a many-body system with components such as mesons, pions, and quarks. His work resulted in the "Koltun Sum Rule" which was used in measurement of electron scattering from nuclear targets.<ref name=Sierra/>

He was a visiting staff member at [[Los Alamos Neutron Science Center|Los Alamos Meson Physics Facility]] over a span of 18 years and served on the Facility's Program Advisory Committee.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Koltun |first1=Judith |title=Daniel S. Koltun |journal=Physics Today |date=16 May 2014 |doi=10.1063/PT.5.6061 |url=https://physicstoday.aip.org/obituaries/daniel-s-koltun |access-date=29 June 2026|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He was a visiting fellow at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] and at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]].<ref name=Sierra/> He was a visiting professor from 1976 to 1977 at [[Tel Aviv University]] and in 1985 at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].<ref name=PAW/>

Koltun was awarded the [[Sloan Research Fellowship]], the [[Guggenheim Fellowship]], and the [[NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program|NSF Postdoctoral Fellowship]]. He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name=Sierra/>

He died April 9, 2014, in [[Haverford, Pennsylvania]],<ref name=Sierra>{{cite web |last1=Sierra |first1=Leonor |title=Professor Emeritus of Physics Daniel S. Koltun dies at 80 |url=https://www.rochester.edu/newscenter/professor-emeritus-of-physics-daniel-s-koltun-dies-at-80/ |website=www.rochester.edu |publisher=University of Rochester |access-date=29 June 2026}}</ref> and was interred at [[West Laurel Hill Cemetery]] in [[Bala Cynwyd, Pennsylvania]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Daniel S. Koltun |url=https://remembermyjourney.com/memorials/daniel-s-koltun?id=a4n9G7Ew |website=remembermyjourney.com |publisher=webCemeteries |access-date=27 June 2026}}</ref>
